chunks: for if you meet him, you will find him like an unruly bull whose horns are turned towards its ears. He rides a ferocious riding beast and says it has been tamed.
so tell him: Your maternal cousin says to you
I knew you in the Hijāz and did not know you in Iraq
So, what has dissuaded (you) from what was shown (by you previously)?

key_terms.الحِجَاز: Hijaz, referring to Mecca/Medina where allegiance was previously shown
key_terms.الزُّبَيْر: Az-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, a prominent companion
key_terms.العِرَاق: Iraq, referring to the region of Kufa where the battle took place

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the temperaments of Talhah and Zubayr according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali directs Ibn Abbas to bypass Talhah, whose stubbornness is likened to a bull twisting its horns, and instead engage Zubayr, who is more receptive to counsel. This strategic choice highlights the nuanced political dynamics of the Battle of the Camel, where personal rapport was leveraged to secure obedience. The message underscores the inconsistency in Zubayr's allegiance, contrasting his recognition in the Hijaz with his opposition in Iraq.

en.sayed-ali-raza: If you meet him you will find him like an unruly bull whose horns are turned towards its ears. He rides a ferocious riding beast and says it has been tamed.
Tell him that your maternal cousin says that,
“(It looks as if) in the Hijāz you knew me (accepted me), but (on coming here to) Iraq you do not know me (do not accept me).
So, what has dissuaded (you) from what was shown (by you previously)?!”
